requiredFixes: Rewrite the ## heading to include a plain searchable term: replace 'five-product discovery menu' with 'CTA and navigation changes' or similar — example: 'How Buffer's CTA and Navigation Changes Signal a New Growth Model (2019–2026)'.
Split or trim the paragraph beginning 'Eight navigation items were removed' — it runs ~65 words, exceeding the 60-word cap. Break it into two sentences or remove one idea.

Add an explicit implication sentence at the end of the first H3 block — the current closing sentence explains what Buffer did but not what a founder should infer. Add a one-sentence concrete implication (e.g. what the risk is if a single CTA is retained).
Define 'discovery menu' if it is kept anywhere in the article, or replace it with plain language ('a separate entry point for each product') in the heading.
Move the practical takeaway of the second H3 block into its first sentence — currently the first sentence names a removed element; the implication should be stated first, then the evidence cited.
riskFlags: The claim 'the homepage may no longer be built to convince a skeptical visitor with third-party proof' is inferential from a single CTA removal — hedged with 'may', which is acceptable, but the causal chain from removing 'See All Case Studies →' to 'no longer needs to establish credibility' is a leap; a condition should be attached (e.g. 'if case studies moved to a dedicated page rather than being dropped entirely').

The claim that the CTA expansion 'suggests Buffer no longer expects visitors to arrive knowing which product fits' is plausible but unsupported by session or traffic data — correctly hedged with 'suggests', so no hard penalty, but flagged for transparency.

H3 headings contain 'Buffer's CTAs' and 'Buffer's navigation' — good for internal anchor text and entity relevance.
The Founder Test paragraph includes specific product names (Publish, Create, Community, Analyze, Collaborate, Mobile app, Start page, AI assistant) — these are useful for long-tail entity coverage.
Primary keyword 'Buffer homepage teardown' does not appear in this section — consider one natural mention in the opening or closing sentence.
